column3: Expands the all-encompassing knowledge of heaven and earth to every private gathering and deed.
Sets the nearby eschatological frame in which intercession is unavailable apart from the qualification stated in 2:255.
Directly confirms that intercession benefits only one granted permission and accepted speech.
Joins creation, exhaustive knowledge, and awareness of human deeds to 2:255's cosmic knowledge.
Contrasts a human ruler's claim with the Lord who gives life, causes death, and governs the sun.
Directly states that intercession with Him has no benefit except for one He permits, while naming Him the Most High.
Repeats both knowledge of what lies before and behind people and their lack of comprehensive knowledge.
Extends the verse's exclusive divinity into rejection of false powers and secure faith in God.
Only broadly relates through guidance sought from the one God.
Pairs God's knowledge before and behind creatures with intercession limited to those He approves.
Its parable of ruined charity does not materially explain 2:255.
The encircling punishment statement adds no clear element to 2:255.
Restates possession of heaven and earth and the names Most High, Magnificent.
Shows the protective authority of God over believers against the rival authority of false powers.
Its assurance of unchanging divine words adds little to 2:255.
Portrays God's sustaining restraint over heaven and earth, echoing preservation without weariness.
Demonstrates power to restore life after death, supporting the Living One's unrestricted power.
The guarded sky gives a limited image of divine preservation.
Exactly repeats 2:255's opening confession and the names Living, Self-Subsisting.
Displays restoration of the dead and directs attention to God's might and wisdom.
Affirms that divine bounty is given as He wills and that God is all-encompassing and knowing.
Depicts all in heaven and earth as belonging to Him and unwearied in His worship.
Only loosely echoes God's vastness and knowledge within a charity context.
Affirms God alone as the Real and the Most High, excluding what is invoked besides Him.
Rejects claimed intercessors and grounds the rebuttal in God's knowledge of heaven and earth.
Its reward and freedom from fear concern charitable conduct, not 2:255's claims.
God's creating by His hands and Iblis's pride offer only a remote link to divine exaltedness.
Makes divine communication dependent on His chosen mode and permission, under His high wisdom.
Divine self-sufficiency and forbearance add only a limited attribute connection.
States that God encompasses those who oppose, reinforcing unbounded dominion.
Names the Living, Self-Subsisting and portrays all faces humbled before Him.
The charity parable does not add to the verse's account of God.
The bare phrase about the great news supplies no specific clarification.
Restates exclusive divinity and says His knowledge encompasses everything.
God's sight of deeds provides only a general link to divine knowledge.
Sleep as cessation heightens the contrast with the One untouched by drowsiness or sleep.
The human trust and standing context does not clarify the Self-Subsisting Lord.
States that He gives life, causes death, and gives life again.
Confesses exclusive divinity, reliance on God, and the Lord of the magnificent throne.
God's vast earth and measureless reward are only indirectly related.
Invokes the heaven and earth around people and God's power over them.
Directly contrasts death and sleep under God's control, sharpening 2:255's denial of sleep.
Names Him the Living, denies any god but Him, and calls for exclusive devotion.
Combines giving life to the dead with comprehensive recording and enumeration.
Connects possession of heaven and earth with exclusive divinity and giving life and death.
Its use of guarding and the names High, Great gives only lexical and partial resonance.
Attributes provision, command, life, death, and governance of affairs uniquely to God.
The mention of Solomon's chair does not explain the scope of the Kursi.
Reiterates that worship belongs only to God, supporting the opening exclusivity.
The contrast of divine repentance and human desire adds no clear element.
Sets God's true call against powerless calls to others, reinforcing exclusive divinity.
Rejects partners, children, and uninformed fabrications about the transcendent Creator.
The phrase of capacity supplies no substantive explanation of the Kursi's vastness.
Even harmful acts cannot operate except by God's permission, supporting dependent power.
Teaching expression supplies no specific aid to 2:255.
The desperate absence of intercessors is only an indirect echo of restricted intercession.
A messenger's call is explicitly by God's permission, echoing authorization as a condition.
The reviving of dead earth confirms power to revive the dead and power over all things.
Treats intercession as accountable action under God's comprehensive reckoning.
God's supreme name gives only a general link to His exaltedness.
The request for a clear thing does not clarify 2:255.
Limited divine encompassing knowledge in a narrative scene only faintly echoes 2:255.
God alone judges by truth while those invoked besides Him judge nothing.
The statement of excellent character does not add to 2:255.
Longing for life and God's sight of deeds offer only a remote contrast to the Living One.
The guarded tablet gives a limited preservation motif without clarifying 2:255.
God's guidance by permission adds only a broad authorization theme.
Condemns claiming falsehood without encompassing its knowledge, echoing human non-encompassment.
Explicitly says the Lord's knowledge encompasses every thing.
Its praise of patience and great fortune does not explain 2:255.
Its closing claim that God teaches and knows all things is general and contextually remote.
States that even many angels' intercession avails only after God's permission and approval.
Names God as Creator of earth and the high heavens, supporting cosmic dominion.
Concise affirmation that He alone causes death and gives life.
God's sight of deeds in a particular conflict adds little to 2:255.
The oath by the even and odd gives no clear explanatory value.
States that the Lord's knowledge encompasses every thing and subjects return to His will.
Human lack of encompassing knowledge is present, but only in a narrative admonition.
The duration of Noah's mission and flood do not clarify 2:255.
A guardian over every soul is too unspecified to explain God's preservation of heaven and earth.
The teaching by one mighty in power does not clarify 2:255.
Questions taking intercessors that neither possess anything nor understand.
Distinguishes the messenger from a guardian or agent, only indirectly reserving ultimate guardianship to God.
The declaration of great success does not clarify 2:255.
Obedience to a commanded act under God's will is only remotely connected.
The messenger is not made a guardian over rejecters, a limited indirect contrast.
Attributes unseen knowledge exclusively to God and specifies exhaustive knowledge of every occurrence.
Faults people for denying what they have not encompassed in knowledge.
Reserves knowledge of the Hour to God alone and stresses its weight over heaven and earth.
God's presence and preservation of deeds offer only a general link.
Restates possession of heaven and earth and connects it with comprehensive recompense.
Affirms God's highest likeness and His might and wisdom, supporting transcendence.
The ordered creation, death, and revivification of life and earth supports divine power.
The covenant's command to worship none but God reinforces exclusive divinity.
Rejects deifying others and contrasts creaturely knowledge with God's knowledge of the unseen.
Combines creation and governance with the rule that no intercessor acts except after His permission.
Charitable reward and freedom from fear do not materially explain 2:255.
Denies spouse and child to the exalted Lord, reinforcing divine transcendence.
The contrast between God's way and false power is too general to explain 2:255.
Growth of land by the Lord's permission gives only a remote image of divine governance.
Affirms God's kingdom over heaven and earth and denies any protector or helper besides Him.
Attributes east and west to God and names Him all-encompassing and knowing.
Rejects the claim of a child and declares all in heaven and earth devoted to Him.
Restates exclusive divinity in a concentrated confession of the one God.
Restates possession of heaven and earth and God's knowledge of what people disclose or conceal.
States that nothing in earth or heaven is hidden from God.
Attributes formation in the wombs to God as He wills, under His might and wisdom.
Witnesses to God's exclusive divinity together with angels and those possessing knowledge.
Affirms that all sovereignty, honor, abasement, and good are in God's hand.
Restates that whatever is in heaven and earth belongs to God and all affairs return to Him.
Attributes the dominion of heaven and earth and power over every thing to God.
Restates possession of heaven and earth and God's encompassing reality.
Restates God's possession of all in heaven and earth and His self-sufficiency.
Again assigns everything in heaven and earth to God and calls Him sufficient as guardian.
Rejects a divine child, affirms God's ownership of heaven and earth, and names Him sufficient guardian.
Affirms God's sovereignty over heaven and earth, creation as He wills, and power over every thing.
States God's dominion over heaven and earth, His judgment, and power over every thing.
Attributes the kingdom of heaven, earth, and all within them to God and affirms His power over every thing.
Names Him God in heaven and earth and affirms knowledge of what people conceal and reveal.
Names Him the subduer above His servants, with wisdom and full awareness.
Describes God as subduer over His servants and sender of preserving keepers.
Names God knower of the unseen and witnessed, with sovereign command.
Rejects a child and identifies the Originator of heaven and earth as knower of every thing.
Affirms exclusive worship of the Creator of every thing and calls Him guardian over every thing.
Denies that vision encompasses Him while affirming that He encompasses all vision.
Combines creation, command, cosmic ordering, and blessed lordship over the worlds.
Names God as protector and the one who brings the righteous into care.
Restates God's dominion over heaven and earth and His giving life and death.
Restates that all in heaven and earth belongs to God and that His promise is true.
Affirms that no smallest matter in earth or heaven escapes God's knowledge.
States that none can remove harm or withhold mercy except God, who grants bounty as He wills.
Reserves the unseen of heaven and earth to God and directs all affairs back to Him.
Combines creation of heaven and earth, exaltation, and governance of the affair.
States God's knowledge of every womb and that all things are measured with Him.
Names Him knower of unseen and witnessed, the Great and Most High.
Portrays willing and unwilling submission of all in heaven and earth to God.
Asks who is Lord of heaven and earth and rejects partners who control neither benefit nor harm.
Depicts every creature in heaven and earth, including angels, prostrating without pride.
Affirms that enduring devotion belongs to God alone and that He alone is to be feared.
Attributes creation, death, and the return from knowledge to ignorance to God.
Reserves the unseen of heaven and earth to God and affirms His power over it.
Rejects additional gods by showing that they would seek a way against the Lord of the Throne.
Portrays the seven heavens, earth, and all within them glorifying Him.
Denies child, partner, and protecting ally to God, then commands His magnification.
Ascribes complete knowledge of the unseen of heaven and earth to God and denies any partner in His judgment.
Names Him Lord of heaven and earth and all between them, worthy of worship without equal name.
Restates that there is no god but Him and assigns to Him the most beautiful names.
Names God the True King and the Most High.
Argues that multiple gods in heaven and earth would cause their corruption, exalting the Lord of the Throne.
Distinguishes God's unanswerable action from creatures who are questioned.
Rejects the claim that God has taken a child and portrays honored servants under His command.
States that the servants do not precede Him in speech and act only by His command.
Depicts widespread prostration in heaven and earth under God's authority.
States that God knows all in heaven and earth and that this is held in a record.
Declares that people have not estimated God as He deserves and names Him strong and mighty.
Identifies the earth and all within it as belonging to God.
Names God Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the magnificent throne.
Attributes dominion over every thing and protection without any protection against Him to God.
Rejects child and partner and describes the incoherence of divided divinity.
Restates that the dominion of heaven and earth belongs to God and that to Him is the return.
Restates God's possession of heaven and earth and His complete knowledge of every human state.
Affirms the kingdom of heaven and earth, denies child and partner, and attributes measured creation to God.
Names the revealer as knower of the secret of heaven and earth.
Directs reliance to the Living One who does not die.
Restates exclusive divinity and names God Lord of the magnificent throne.
Reserves knowledge of the unseen in heaven and earth to God alone.
Restates exclusive divinity and assigns praise, judgment, and return to God.
Denies any god besides Him and affirms His enduring reality, judgment, and final return.
Links confession of the Creator and subjector of heaven and earth to recognition of God.
Attributes sending water, reviving earth, and provision to God.
States that all in heaven and earth belongs to God and is devoutly obedient to Him.
Attributes origination and repetition of creation to God and names Him Most High in heaven and earth.
Restates that all in heaven and earth belongs to God, who is self-sufficient and praiseworthy.
Combines creation of heaven and earth, exaltation over the Throne, and denial of any protector or intercessor besides Him.
Attributes governance of the affair from heaven to earth to God.
Reserves knowledge of the Hour to God alone.
Attributes all in heaven and earth to God and names Him wise and fully aware.
States exhaustive knowledge of all that enters and leaves earth and descends from or ascends to heaven.
Asserts that not even an atom in heaven or earth escapes the Knower of the unseen.
Denies that those invoked besides God possess even an atom, share, or supporting role in heaven and earth.
States that none can withhold God's opened mercy or release what He withholds.
Identifies God as the Creator and provider from heaven and earth, with no god besides Him.
Names God knower of the unseen of heaven and earth and of what breasts conceal.
Argues that the Creator of heaven and earth is fully able to create their like.
Attributes the dominion of every thing to God and the final return to Him.
Restates that the God addressed is one.
Names Him Lord of heaven, earth, and all between them.
Glorifies the Lord of might above what people ascribe to Him.
Restates exclusive divinity and names God the One, the Subduer.
Assigns all intercession to God and joins it to His dominion over heaven and earth.
Identifies God as Creator of every thing and guardian over every thing.
Attributes the keys of heaven and earth to God.
Describes the earth in His grasp and heavens folded in His right hand, exalting Him above partners.
Names Him exalted in degrees and Lord of the Throne, who sends the spirit by His command.
Attributes the fashioned earth, built heaven, provision, and lordship over the worlds to God.
Forbids worship of sun and moon and directs worship to their Creator.
Reserves knowledge of the Hour to God and affirms His knowledge of every emerging and conceiving thing.
Denies any likeness to God while naming Him the Hearing, Seeing.
Attributes the keys of heaven and earth and the measure of provision to God.
Restates God's dominion over heaven and earth and His creation as He wills.
Names Him God in heaven and God on earth, the Wise and Knowing.
Attributes blessing, dominion of heaven and earth, and knowledge of the Hour to God.
Assigns all greatness in heaven and earth to God, the Mighty and Wise.
Argues that the unwearied Creator of heaven and earth has power to give life to the dead.
Restates God's dominion over heaven and earth and His authority to forgive or punish.
Explicitly denies that creation of heaven and earth brought God any weariness.
Attributes construction and vast extension of heaven to God's power.
States God's complete knowledge of people from their origin in earth and their formation in wombs.
Affirms that every thing is created by measure.
Portrays all in heaven and earth glorifying God and names Him Mighty and Wise.
Names Him First, Last, Manifest, Hidden, and knowing of every thing.
Restates dominion of heaven and earth and the return of all affairs to God.
Names God as the only god, knower of unseen and witnessed.
Names the only God as King, Holy, Peace, Guardian, Mighty, Compeller, and Supreme.
Names God Creator, Originator, Fashioner, to whom the names belong and whom all creation glorifies.
Portrays all in heaven and earth glorifying the King, Holy, Mighty, Wise.
Portrays all in heaven and earth glorifying God, to whom belong dominion and praise and power over every thing.
States God's knowledge of all in heaven and earth, what people conceal or reveal, and what breasts contain.
Links seven heavens and earth with descending command so people know God's power and encompassing knowledge.
Attributes all dominion to God and affirms His power over every thing.
Attributes knowledge of the unseen to the forgiving Lord.
States that God knows both concealed and spoken speech and what breasts contain.
States that the Creator knows, while naming Him subtle and fully aware.
Names God knower of the unseen who discloses it to no one except a chosen messenger.
States that God encompasses what is with His messengers and counts every thing.
Restates that God is one.
Names God the Self-Sufficient Refuge, reinforcing His independence.
Denies begetting and being begotten.
Denies any equal or comparable being to God.
